youtube_title: Why Does a Diwali Bonus Even Exist? 🪔 #Shorts
youtube_description:
Diwali bonus aaya! But why is it even a thing?

The popular story: under the British, workers were paid weekly, 52 weeks a year. When pay went monthly, 12 months = 48 weeks of pay, so 4 weeks were 'lost'. After protests, in 1940 a '13th month' pay was given around Diwali. In 1965 India made bonus a law, the Payment of Bonus Act (now part of the Code on Wages): for eligible employees, minimum 8.33% of yearly wages (= one month out of 12), maximum 20%.

Rule: split it before it lands. Clear card dues first, a fixed part for Diwali, the rest to savings.
Moral: A bonus is a reward, not a reason to go broke.

Sources: Payment of Bonus Act, 1965; DailyO.
